Here is the full report.

---

# AXEL Chat Efficiency Audit Report

## 1. Transcript Bloat Profile

**Sample:** [Combat item plan + implement](af36930b-e3fd-49df-80f4-67094ef80d10) -- 43 messages, 6 todos, consumed full context window.

### Bloat patterns found

**A. Repeated status-template overhead.**
The governance rule (items 7-8) requires a 6-field progress block every turn: current step, tool running, files being checked, result/status, next step, stuck state. This block appeared in roughly 15 assistant turns at ~120 tokens each = ~1,800 tokens of pure template repetition across the chat. During dense implementation stretches (editing GDScript files, fixing lints), these blocks add no value -- the tool calls themselves show what's happening.

**B. Long visible "thinking aloud" blocks.**
Turn 9 in the transcript contains an enormous pre-tool reasoning block (~2,000+ tokens) where the assistant narrates design forks, edge case analysis, rarity color choices, equip-limit tradeoffs, self-corrections, and implementation strategy -- all before issuing any tool calls. Much of this reasoning was already decided in the plan and didn't need to be re-derived in the implementation turn.

**C. Large tool payloads accumulating in context.**
The full `StrReplace` of `item_inventory.gd` (turn 11), the full `Write` of `item_synergy_smoke.gd` (~200 lines, turn 23), and the massive changelog entry (turn 37) all became part of the conversation context. Each subsequent turn carries all prior tool payloads.

**D. Duplicate end-of-chat summary.**
Turn 40 re-explains all 6 completed todos in a formatted summary, despite the changelog entry (turn 37) already documenting everything. The last turn (43) also repeats catalog info when answering a follow-up question, duplicating content already in context.

**E. TodoWrite content repetition.**
Every `TodoWrite` call repeats the full content string of each todo. Across 6 todos with ~12 status flips, this adds ~1,500 tokens of repeated todo text.

**Contrast with stub chat:** The current chat (ef94eb64) had only 1 user turn with no accumulated bloat, confirming the problem is proportional to chat length and implementation density, not baseline setup.

---

## 2. Repo Hotspot Inventory

| Path | Size | Risk | How it gets pulled in |
|------|------|------|----------------------|
| `logs/debug/debug-1d1bdd.log` | **303 MB** | Critical | Any search/read that touches `logs/` or accidental semantic index hit |
| `logs/debug/debug-c9d495.log` | **71 MB** | Critical | Same |
| `AXEL/.../moon_princess_files/moonprincess100_mobile.bundle.js` | **2.57 MB** | High | Semantic search, broad codebase reads, or `@exports/` references |
| `AXEL/.../moon_princess_files/ContainerLauncher_bundle.js` | **434 KB** | High | Same |
| `AXEL/.../moon_princess_files/mobile_videoslot.css` | **417 KB** | Medium | Same |
| `AXEL/.../plans/scenes/AXEL_SCENES_NEW.md` | **998 lines** | Medium | Scene agent reads full file; any narrative task that touches scenes |
| `AXEL/.../plans/qa/AXEL_QA_RUN_LOG.md` | **254 lines** (growing) | Low-Medium | QA runs read full log; grows linearly |

**Critical finding: No `.cursorignore` file exists.** This means Cursor's index includes the 303 MB debug log, the 2.57 MB JS bundle, and all other large files. Any semantic search, codebase-wide grep, or accidental `@` reference can pull these into context.

---

## 3. Duplication Map

### 3a. Governance rule vs AI_DOCS (near-complete duplication)

The governance rule (`axel-ai-docs-governance.mdc`, 41 lines) is an **always-injected** system prompt that duplicates nearly every section of `AI_DOCS.md` (203 lines):

| Governance items | AI_DOCS section | Content | Classification |
|-----------------|----------------|---------|---------------|
| Item 1 | Section 9, item 1 | "Read AI_DOCS first" | **Required** (this is the pointer) |
| Items 2-3 | Sections 3, 5 | Hierarchy + terminology | **Avoidable** |
| Item 4 | Section 4 | Moon princess = reference-only | **Avoidable** |
| Items 5-6 | Section 9, items 5,7 | Changelog + conflict resolution | **Avoidable** |
| Items 7-8 | Section 9, items 3-4 | Live progress feed (6-field format) | **Avoidable** |
| Item 9 | Section 9, item 8 | Reusable workflow update | **Avoidable** |
| Items 10-15 | Section 11 | Scene agent + QA aliases + invariants | **Avoidable** |
| Items 16-19 | Section 10 | Premium planning + intent-deduction + conflict gate | **Avoidable** |
| Item 20 | Section 11 | Bot playthrough details | **Avoidable** |
| Item 21 | Section 5 | Item catalog pointer | **Avoidable** |

**Result:** Out of 21 governance items, only item 1 ("read AI_DOCS first") is the essential pointer. Items 2-21 duplicate content that agents will read when they follow item 1. This means ~95% of the governance rule is redundant once AI_DOCS is loaded.

**Token cost:** The governance rule is injected into the system prompt of every single turn. On a 43-turn chat, that's 41 lines x 43 turns = ~1,763 redundant line-impressions across the conversation.

### 3b. QA command set (quadruple duplication)

The 6 headless commands + item_balance_audit + persistence invariant appear in:

1. `axel-ai-docs-governance.mdc` (items 11, 13) -- always injected
2. `AI_DOCS.md` (section 11, lines 168-173) -- read on first turn
3. `SKILL.md` (lines 42-54, 78-89) -- read when QA is triggered
4. `AXEL_QA_REVIEW_RUBRIC.md` (lines 18-36, 170-189) -- read when QA is triggered

**In a QA run, all four are loaded.** The rubric (193 lines) is the canonical source. The other three copies are redundant overhead.

### 3c. Bot playthrough details (triple duplication)

The `InputEventKey`-based bot description appears in governance (item 20), AI_DOCS (section 11, lines 174-181), and the QA rubric (confidence tiers). Canonical source should be `test/bots/README.md` or the rubric.

### 3d. Scene agent invariants (double duplication)

Canonical filename invariant and cleanup invariant appear in governance (items 14-15) and AI_DOCS (section 11, lines 151-160).

---

## 4. Impact Ranking

### HIGH priority (safe, immediate, high savings)

| # | Recommendation | Est. savings | Risk | Reversible |
|---|---------------|-------------|------|-----------|
| H1 | **Create `.cursorignore`** to exclude `logs/debug/**`, `AXEL/**/moon_princess_files/**`, `**/*.bundle.js` | Prevents 303 MB + 2.57 MB from entering index/context | None | Yes |
| H2 | **Slim governance rule to pointer-only** -- keep items 1, 12 (QA opt-in trigger), 18 (hard conflict gate); replace items 2-11, 13-17, 19-21 with "see AI_DOCS.md" | ~35 lines removed from every turn's system prompt | Very low -- agents still read AI_DOCS per item 1 | Yes |
| H3 | **Relax progress feed to 1-line during implementation** -- the 6-field template is useful during planning/exploration but pure overhead during dense edit stretches. Change items 7-8 to "required for planning/exploration turns; one-line status sufficient during implementation" | ~1,800 tokens saved across a 43-turn implementation chat | Slightly less visibility, but tool calls already show what's happening | Yes |

### MEDIUM priority (needs doc synchronization)

| # | Recommendation | Est. savings | Risk | Reversible |
|---|---------------|-------------|------|-----------|
| M1 | **Unify QA command references** -- keep full command lists only in `AXEL_QA_REVIEW_RUBRIC.md`. Replace duplicates in AI_DOCS (section 11) and SKILL.md with "see rubric section Playtest-mode" | ~400 lines of duplicate content across 4 files reduced to ~50 lines of pointers | If agent skips rubric read, it loses detail. Mitigated: governance still requires rubric read | Yes |
| M2 | **Consolidate bot playthrough details** -- keep in rubric + `test/bots/README.md` only | ~100 lines of duplicate content | Same as M1 | Yes |
| M3 | **Split `AXEL_SCENES_NEW.md` by arc** -- create per-arc files (`AXEL_SCENES_ARC1.md`, etc.) and keep the 998-line file as a short TOC | Scene agent loads only the arc it needs instead of 998 lines | Requires updating scene agent spec references | Yes |

### LOW priority (optional hygiene)

| # | Recommendation | Est. savings | Risk | Reversible |
|---|---------------|-------------|------|-----------|
| L1 | **Archive debug logs** -- `logs/debug/debug-1d1bdd.log` (303 MB) and `debug-c9d495.log` (71 MB) serve no active agent purpose | Frees disk, reduces accidental reads | None if they're regenerated by Godot | Yes |
| L2 | **QA run log archival** -- move bulk JSON history to `qa/archive/*.json`, keep only last 5 entries in main log | Prevents log from growing unboundedly | Requires updating `update_qa_analytics.py` to scan archive | Yes |
| L3 | **Consider splitting plan from implement chats** -- start a fresh chat for implementation with a short pointer to the plan, rather than carrying the full planning context through 30+ edit turns | Avoids carrying plan+reads through every implementation turn | Requires manual discipline | N/A |

Implement the three HIGH-priority recommendations: add `.cursorignore` fences, slim the always-applied governance rule to pointer-first guidance, and relax mandatory progress-feed verbosity during implementation loops.
- Motivation: The audit ([Chat efficiency audit](ef94eb64-2da7-4be5-b1ef-a1704d663ee0)) found that the governance rule duplicated ~95% of `AI_DOCS.md` content (injected into every turn's system prompt), no `.cursorignore` existed (allowing 303 MB debug logs and 2.5 MB JS bundles into the index), and the rigid 6-field progress template added ~1,800 tokens of repetitive overhead across a 43-turn implementation chat.
- Implementation:
  - Created `.cursorignore` with three narrow exclusion patterns: `logs/debug/**`, `AXEL/axel_project/exports/moon_princess_files/**`, `**/*bundle*.js`.
  - Refactored `axel-ai-docs-governance.mdc` from 42 lines of duplicated detail to 16 lines of pointer-first guidance. Preserved in-rule: read-AI_DOCS directive, hard conflict gate, QA opt-in trigger, canonical alias stability, and pipeline discovery hook. Removed: duplicated QA command matrices, scene/bot implementation details, premium planning checklists, terminology locks, and other content already in `AI_DOCS.md`.
  - Updated progress-feed policy in both governance rule and `AI_DOCS.md` §9: full structured format for planning/exploration/blocked states; concise one-liner sufficient during dense implementation loops.
  - Added governance responsibility split note to `AI_DOCS.md` §9 to prevent future re-expansion drift.
- Files changed:
  - `.cursorignore` (new)
  - `.cursor/rules/axel-ai-docs-governance.mdc`
  - `AXEL/axel_project/plans/core/AI_DOCS.md`
  - `AXEL/axel_project/plans/core/AI_CHANGELOG.md`
- Behavior impact: No gameplay/canon/runtime changes. Agent context overhead reduced: ~35 lines removed from every turn's system prompt; 375 MB of files excluded from indexing; progress-feed overhead reduced during implementation stretches.
- Verification: Governance rule still enforces conflict gate, QA opt-in, canonical aliases, and AI_DOCS-first read. AI_DOCS.md retains all detailed procedures, invariants, and pipeline specs. `.cursorignore` patterns are narrow and exclude only non-authoritative artifacts.
- Rollback: Restore prior governance rule body from git history. Remove `.cursorignore` to re-index excluded files. Revert `AI_DOCS.md` §9 progress-feed wording and responsibility-split note.

content.text:
All six todos are complete. Here's what was done:

**`.cursorignore` (new)** -- Fences off 375 MB of irrelevant content from Cursor's index: debug logs, Moon Princess reference JS bundles, and any stray bundle files.

**`axel-ai-docs-governance.mdc`** -- Reduced from 42 lines to 16 lines of content. Kept the four critical safeguards (read AI_DOCS first, hard conflict gate, QA opt-in, canonical aliases). Replaced all duplicated QA command matrices, scene/bot details, premium planning checklists, and terminology locks with concise pointers to the relevant AI_DOCS sections where that content already lives.

**`AI_DOCS.md` section 9** -- Updated progress-feed policy to allow one-liner status during dense implementation (full format still required for planning/exploration/blocked states). Added a responsibility-split note at the bottom of the section to prevent future agents from re-duplicating detailed content back into the governance rule.

**`AI_CHANGELOG.md`** -- Full entry with motivation, changes, behavior impact confirmation, and explicit rollback instructions.

All changes are reversible via git history if anything feels wrong. No gameplay, canon, or runtime behavior was touched.
